# What is Google friendly JavaScript

Day 2, 11:15 · Erin Sparling, Partner Technology Manager · coverage: transcript, slides, video

Same speaker as the opener of Lightning session D.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Google renders nearly all of the web by replicating what a browser does, using a real browser's rendering engine.
  > "Google renders nearly all of the internet by replicating browser actions"
  <br><sub>`D2-C256` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extended by [D3-C628](D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's JavaScript SEO basics says every page with a 200 status code is queued for rendering, whether or not it uses JavaScript, unless a robots meta tag or header says not to index it; for non-200 pages such as 404 error pages, rendering might be skipped.
  <br><sub>`D2-C257` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Stage]** If JavaScript rendering fails, what Google indexes for a page differs from what the page shows once it is rendered.
  <br><sub>`D2-C258` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Erin Sparling named server-side or hybrid rendering, fallbacks and not leaving placeholders in the DOM, among other measures, as ways to guard against failed JavaScript rendering.
  <br><sub>`D2-C259` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Extends [D2-C149](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-06`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google listed four common JavaScript problems for indexing: content not present in the rendered HTML, using # in URLs for content changes, soft 404s and blocked resources.
  <br><sub>`D2-C260` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's slide called content missing from the rendered HTML the most common JavaScript issue for indexing.
  > "The most common issue."
  <br><sub>`D2-C261` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-REN-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Content that is not in the final DOM after rendering cannot be seen by Google, so it cannot be indexed.
  > "If it's not in the final DOM, Google can't see it."
  <br><sub>`D2-C262` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Repeats [D2-C174](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Content is missing from the rendered HTML either because the server does not serve it or because the content has still not appeared after some period of time.
  <br><sub>`D2-C263` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C149](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-06`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's slide defined a soft 404 in a JavaScript application as a page that serves a 'Not Found' message but returns a 200 HTTP status code.
  > "Your application serves a "Not Found" message but returns a 200 HTTP status code."
  <br><sub>`D2-C264` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Repeats [D1-C073](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Blocked resources, one of Google's four common JavaScript indexing problems, means robots.txt disallowing the crawling of critical JavaScript files or API endpoints.
  > "robots.txt disallowing crawling of critical .js or API endpoints."
  <br><sub>`D2-C265` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Introduction to robots.txt](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro) · Repeats [D2-C204](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-04`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google named three causes of content missing from the rendered HTML: JavaScript inaccessible to Googlebot, JavaScript DOM event triggers and disabled browser APIs.
  <br><sub>`D2-C266` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript)</sub>

- **[Stage]** When the JavaScript is not accessible to Googlebot, Google cannot render the client-side DOM that the page builds asynchronously, so parts of the page may be present while the main content is absent.
  <br><sub>`D2-C267` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Content that loads only when a user clicks an element is not supported in the way Google renders pages for indexing.
  <br><sub>`D2-C268` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading), [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Extends [D1-C115](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Repeats [D2-C195](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-02`, the glossary term *Lazy loading*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Browser APIs that need user permission, such as payments and location, are not supported when Google renders a page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C269` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Used by `DEV-REN-08`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google said there is no single fix for content missing from the rendered HTML: the solution varies by case, and the advice is to follow best practices.
  > "Solution: varies by case, but follow best practices."
  <br><sub>`D2-C270` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google does not scroll a page when it renders it for indexing, so content that infinite scroll loads on scroll-depth triggers works for users but is never loaded for Google.
  <br><sub>`D2-C271` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading) · Extends [D1-C114](D1-S12-q-a.md) · Repeats [D2-C197](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extends [D1-C491](D1-S12-q-a.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-03`, `DEV-URL-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Instead of scrolling, Google renders a page in a very tall viewport, around 10,000 pixels high.
  > "it renders it in a very tall viewport. Specifically, around 10,000 pixels is what the viewport gets rendered as."
  <br><sub>`D2-C272` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C199](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-03`, `DEV-URL-07`, the glossary term *Viewport expansion*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's March 2023 SEO office hours say Google sees infinite-scroll content through viewport expansion, rendering a page like a very long phone, which is not particularly efficient and can miss infinite content.
  > "a technique called "viewport expansion", where we render a page like a very long phone"
  <br><sub>`D2-C273` · Google Search Central (SEO office hours transcript, March 2023) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [March 2023 Google SEO office hours](https://developers.google.com/search/help/office-hours/2023/march) · Used by `DEV-URL-07`, the glossary term *Viewport expansion*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Content loaded as elements enter the viewport, for example with an Intersection Observer, does load when Google renders a page, because Google's rendering viewport is very tall.
  <br><sub>`D2-C274` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading) · Repeats [D2-C199](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-03`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Treat the 10,000-pixel viewport as a safety margin, not a target: load lazy content when it enters the viewport (Intersection Observer or native lazy loading, never scroll listeners), and give infinite-scroll content paginated URLs linked with `<a href>` so anything below the first rendered screen stays reachable.
  <br><sub>`D2-C275` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript</sub>

- **[Docs]** To make infinite scroll indexable, Google's lazy-loading guide says to support paginated loading: give each chunk its own persistent, unique URL, link sequentially to those URLs, and update the displayed URL with the History API when a new chunk becomes the main visible element.
  <br><sub>`D2-C276` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading) · Extends [D1-C115](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** WebGL does not work well in Google's rendering: a WebGL shader that makes a page look like it is underwater will not be applied when Google renders the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C277` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Used by `DEV-REN-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** For effects that need WebGL, which Googlebot does not support, Google's guide to fixing JavaScript problems suggests skipping the effect or prerendering it with server-side rendering so that the content is accessible to Googlebot.
  <br><sub>`D2-C278` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Used by `DEV-REN-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Erin Sparling recommended differential serving and polyfills to keep a site compatible with Google's rendering engine where it lacks a browser feature.
  <br><sub>`D2-C279` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's JavaScript SEO basics recommends differential serving and polyfills when feature detection finds a missing browser API, and warns that some browser features cannot be polyfilled.
  > "We recommend using differential serving and polyfills if you feature-detect a missing browser API that you need."
  <br><sub>`D2-C280` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Used by `DEV-REN-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Polyfills work in two directions: they patch backwards where a browser lacks support, or patch forward to build now for a feature expected in the future, as Web Fragments does.
  <br><sub>`D2-C281` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C254](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Wrap permission-based features (location, payments, camera) and WebGL effects in feature detection with a fallback, so the main content renders when the API is missing or the permission is declined; never make indexable content wait for a permission prompt.
  <br><sub>`D2-C282` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · Used by `DEV-REN-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Erin Sparling called URL fragments (the part of a URL after #) the next most common JavaScript issue seen, after rendering problems and blocked rendering.
  <br><sub>`D2-C283` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** URL fragments (#) are often ignored by crawlers: a fragment exists only in the browser, so Google cannot request it.
  > "Fragment identifiers (#) are often ignored by crawlers."
  <br><sub>`D2-C284` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript), [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Repeats [D1-C101](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-03`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google recommends the History API to give single-page apps clean URLs instead of fragment-based routes.
  > "Use the History API for clean URLs in SPAs."
  <br><sub>`D2-C285` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Repeats [D2-C185](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-03`, the glossary term *History API*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Moving a single-page app from fragment-based routes to real paths with the History API keeps the same client-side behaviour and was described as not free but relatively straightforward.
  <br><sub>`D2-C286` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Used by `DEV-URL-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A link that is an `<a>` element but does not point to a real URL gives Google something to look at, but Google will not know where the link goes.
  <br><sub>`D2-C287` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable), [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D1-C040](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extends [D2-C040](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** With the History API, a single-page app can use real links and attach event listeners that intercept the click, rewrite the URL with pushState and load the new content, so Google can follow the links while users avoid full page reloads.
  <br><sub>`D2-C288` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D2-C185](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-03`, the glossary term *History API*, the glossary term *Single-page app (SPA)*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Real URLs also work as deep links: Android, iOS and desktop operating systems accept full URLs as keys to specific content in an app, so clean URLs simplify the cross-platform user experience, not only indexing.
  <br><sub>`D2-C289` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-URL-03`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Audit a single-page app by searching both the templates and the rendered HTML for href="#..." routes, `<a>` elements without href and onclick navigation; every view that should rank needs an `<a href>` link to a real path.
  <br><sub>`D2-C290` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript</sub>

- **[Stage]** In JavaScript single-page apps, soft 404s typically arise because the server returns the app with a 200 status for every URL, so when the app shows a 'not found' message for a URL that does not exist, no error is reported.
  <br><sub>`D2-C291` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript), [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D1-C073](D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Repeats [D2-C190](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** The fix for a client-side soft 404 is to serve a real 404 error page where appropriate; how to detect URLs that do not exist depends on how the app works and where it is hosted.
  <br><sub>`D2-C292` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D2-C191](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In an app routed with the History API, when a user reaches a page that does not exist, Erin Sparling suggested asking how they got there and redirecting to a real 404 page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C293` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript)</sub>

- **[Docs]** For client-side rendered single-page apps, where meaningful status codes can be impossible or impractical, Google's documentation gives two ways to avoid soft 404s: a JavaScript redirect to a URL that returns a 404 status, or a noindex robots meta tag added with JavaScript.
  <br><sub>`D2-C294` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Used by `DEV-ERR-02`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** After moving to real paths, set the server or hosting rewrite rules so a direct request to every valid path returns 200 with the content (ideally server-rendered) and an unknown path returns a 404 status, which removes client-side soft 404s at the source.
  <br><sub>`D2-C295` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · Used by `DEV-ERR-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** If robots.txt blocks JavaScript that client-side code needs to render, Google cannot render the content that the JavaScript would produce.
  <br><sub>`D2-C296` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D1-C064](D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Repeats [D2-C204](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-04`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's introduction to robots.txt says unimportant image, script or style files may be blocked, but resources whose absence makes a page harder for Google to understand should not be blocked.
  <br><sub>`D2-C297` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Introduction to robots.txt](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro) · Used by `DEV-REN-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Check robots.txt for Disallow rules covering JavaScript bundles, build folders or API endpoints the page calls while rendering, including on separate API or CDN hostnames with their own robots.txt, then confirm in URL Inspection's live test that the rendered HTML contains the main content.
  <br><sub>`D2-C298` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript</sub>

- **[Stage]** A headless content management system serves its content as an API; even WordPress, often seen as one monolithic application, can be used headless, with only its editor or only its renderer.
  <br><sub>`D2-C299` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Erin Sparling's practice with a headless CMS is to give an AI agent the content's JSON Schema and have it build a throwaway prototype front end, to see the content before deciding how to render it; the prototype is not meant for launch.
  <br><sub>`D2-C300` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For headless CMS content, Erin Sparling presented rendering on the server, not only in the browser, as a way to avoid indexing issues.
  <br><sub>`D2-C301` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [Dynamic rendering as a workaround](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/dynamic-rendering)</sub>

- **[Stage]** When one content schema feeds several front ends (the example was a news UI, then a recipe UI), Erin Sparling had an AI agent add automated browser UI tests and agent controls so the interfaces could be managed and tested.
  <br><sub>`D2-C302` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Combining schema-based interfaces with web standards such as WebMCP lets a site expose tools to AI agents, which can then operate the interfaces, for example to test them.
  <br><sub>`D2-C303` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C281](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** When Search Console reports that content is not rendering, Erin Sparling suggested putting AI agents on the problem, but only after doing your own due diligence.
  <br><sub>`D2-C304` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** With a headless CMS, choose the rendering per template before launch (server-rendered or pre-rendered for pages that must rank), and make any agent-built test suite assert that the main content and `<a href>` links are present in the rendered HTML.
  <br><sub>`D2-C305` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript</sub>

- **[Stage]** To use Search Console to debug what Google can see on a site and why, Erin Sparling said the first step is to get access to the site by verifying ownership (the speaker's words were authorized domains).
  <br><sub>`D2-C306` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · consistent with Google docs · [Verify your site ownership](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9008080?hl=en), [URL Inspection tool](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Erin Sparling showed a Search Console result saying a URL would be indexed only under certain conditions, one of which had not been met, and contrasted it with the result for an available URL whose content loads.
  <br><sub>`D2-C307` · Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript (Erin Sparling) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's URL Inspection help says a valid live test only confirms that Google can access a page for indexing; the page must still meet other conditions to be indexed, such as having no manual action, not being a duplicate and being of high enough quality.
  <br><sub>`D2-C308` · Google Search Console Help · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [URL Inspection tool](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to fixing Search-related JavaScript problems says its Web Rendering Service keeps no state across page loads: local storage, session storage and HTTP cookies are cleared.
  <br><sub>`D2-C828` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Used by `DEV-REN-06`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to fixing Search-related JavaScript problems says the Web Rendering Service may ignore caching headers and so use outdated JavaScript or CSS, and recommends content fingerprinting, which puts a hash of the content in the file name, as in main.2bb85551.js.
  <br><sub>`D2-C829` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Fix Search-related JavaScript problems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/fix-search-javascript) · Used by `DEV-REN-06`</sub>
